entries.text: Thank you for calling VeloFit. Your call may be recorded for quality assurance. Please hold for the next available agent.
Hello, thank you for calling VeloFit support. My name is Isaac. How can I help you today?
I need to return my VeloBand.

I can certainly look into that for you. May I have your name and order number please? ... Thank you. And just to be sure I understand, what specifically is the issue with the band? Is it a technical fault or a preference?
The pulse reading is complete garbage. It's not even close to accurate.

I'm very sorry to hear that. The pulse monitor is a core feature, and I'd be happy to walk you through a couple of quick troubleshooting steps. Sometimes a simple reset or a fit adjustment can fix that right up.
Listen, I really don't have time for all that. The product doesn't work as advertised. I just want my money back.
I understand your frustration. For a defect claim like this, our standard process is to connect you with technical support to verify the fault. It's usually very quick.
No. I'm not playing games with tech support. I want a refund. It's a simple request.
Okay, I hear you. You're not interested in troubleshooting. Let me pull up your order details and review the return eligibility. One moment... Okay, I see the item was delivered 24 days ago.
Alright, I've checked our policy. It states that items can be returned within 90 days of delivery. Since you're well within that window, I can go ahead and approve this return for you.
Fine. Whatever. Just send the information.

Of course. I've just processed the return authorization. You'll receive an email with a prepaid shipping label and instructions within the next 10 minutes. Once we receive the band at our facility, the refund will be issued to your original payment method. Can I help with anything else?
